Yes — Bangladeshi passport holders need a visa. You'll apply for the C-3-9 short-term tourist visa (single entry, stay up to 90 days). Fill the e-Form on visa.go.kr, print the barcoded form, and submit it in person at the Korean Embassy in Dhaka. K-ETA/visa-free entry does NOT apply to Bangladeshi passports.

faq.q: Do Bangladeshi citizens need a visa for Korea?
faq.a: Yes — for tourism you apply in advance for the C-3-9 short-term tourist visa. Bangladeshi passports are not visa-free and not on the K-ETA list.

faq.q: Where do I apply?
faq.a: You fill the e-Form on the Korea Visa Portal (visa.go.kr) and submit the printed, barcoded form in person at the Korean Embassy in Dhaka (4 Madani Avenue, Baridhara).

faq.q: What is the e-Form?
faq.a: Since 2026 every applicant must complete the online e-Form on visa.go.kr and print it — the printout has a barcode that the embassy scans. Handwritten old forms are not accepted.

faq.q: How long does it take?
faq.a: Usually about 10–15 working days, and longer during peak season or if you're called for an interview or extra documents. Apply well ahead of your trip.

faq.q: How much does it cost?
faq.a: About US$40 for a single-entry short-term visa; roughly US$70 for double entry and US$90 for multiple entry. Amounts change — confirm the current fee at the embassy.

faq.q: What is a Bank Solvency Certificate?
faq.a: A letter from your bank confirming you are financially solvent. Bangladesh applicants are usually expected to submit it in addition to the 6-month bank statement.

faq.q: Can I get a multiple-entry visa?
faq.a: Double- and multiple-entry visas are available for a higher fee, but eligibility varies. Ask at the embassy about current rules for Bangladesh.

faq.q: Do I still need the e-Arrival Card after I get the visa?
faq.a: The e-Arrival Card requirement can still apply on entry. Check the entry-document rules close to your travel date on the official sites.

Yes — Chinese passport holders need a visa for mainland Korea. Individual tourists apply for the C-3 tourist visa at a Korean consulate or Korea Visa Application Center. Two big exceptions can let you skip it: Jeju Island, and (at times) approved group tours.

faq.q: Do Chinese citizens need a visa for Korea?
faq.a: For mainland Korea, yes — individual tourists apply for a C-3 tourist visa. Jeju Island allows visa-free entry up to 30 days, and approved group tours have had time-limited visa-free windows.

faq.q: How does Jeju visa-free work?
faq.a: You can enter Jeju without a visa for up to 30 days, but only on direct flights to and from Jeju — you cannot transit through mainland Korea.

faq.q: Can tour groups still enter visa-free?
faq.a: A trial for approved groups of 3+ ran Sep 2025–Jun 2026. Because such schemes are time-limited, confirm the current status with your travel agency or the embassy.

faq.q: Where do I apply?
faq.a: At the Korea Visa Application Center or Korean consulate for the district where your hukou is registered.

faq.q: How much money do I need to show?
faq.a: No fixed minimum — show a stable 3–6 month balance plus ties to China. Fees are non-refundable.

faq.q: Do I still need the e-Arrival Card?
faq.a: Entry-document rules such as the e-Arrival Card can still apply. Check the current rules near your travel date.

faq.q: How long does a Korea visa take to process?
faq.a: Once your documents are accepted, processing usually takes several business days, though it varies by season and by center. Apply well ahead of your trip and confirm the current turnaround where you apply.

faq.q: Do children need their own Korea visa?
faq.a: Yes — every traveler, including children, needs their own visa. A minor's application is submitted with a parent's supporting documents and proof of the family relationship.

faq.q: What are the most common reasons a Korea visa is refused?
faq.a: Weak or unclear financial proof, an unconvincing trip purpose, incomplete paperwork, or applying at the wrong jurisdiction. Follow the document checklist and apply at the center for your registered address.

Yes — Indian passport holders need a visa. You'll apply for the C-3-9 short-term tourist visa (single entry, stay up to 90 days) in person at a Korea Visa Application Center. K-ETA/visa-free entry does NOT apply to Indian passports.

faq.q: Can Indians get a Korea visa on arrival or e-visa?
faq.a: Not for standard tourism — Indian passport holders apply in advance for the C-3-9 tourist visa at a Korea Visa Application Center. The Korea Visa Portal (visa.go.kr) is where you fill the form; some categories support e-application there.

faq.q: Do I need an appointment?
faq.a: No. In India you can walk in to the KVAC during working hours and submit; no prior appointment is required.

faq.q: How long does it take?
faq.a: Usually about 5–10 working days, but it can be longer during peak travel season or if extra checks are needed. Apply well ahead of your trip.

faq.q: How much does it cost?
faq.a: Roughly INR 3,400 for a single-entry short-term visa, plus the center's service fee (around INR 1,100–1,400). Amounts change — confirm the current fee at your KVAC.

faq.q: Which center do I go to?
faq.a: It depends on your state of residence. South Indian states go through the Chennai jurisdiction (Chennai, Bengaluru); the rest of India goes through the New Delhi/Embassy jurisdiction (New Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and more).

faq.q: Can I get a multiple-entry visa?
faq.a: Multiple-entry tourist visas are possible in some cases (for example applicants with strong travel history), but eligibility varies. Ask at your KVAC or the consulate about current multiple-entry rules for India.

faq.q: What if I've never filed ITR?
faq.a: Submit a signed letter explaining why, and strengthen the file with a solid 6-month bank statement and, if relevant, a sponsor's documents.

faq.q: Do I still need the e-Arrival Card after I get the visa?
faq.a: The e-Arrival Card requirement can still apply on entry. Check the entry-document rules close to your travel date on the official sites.

faq.a: Yes — Nepali documents must be translated into English and notarized. Any Korean documents must be originals issued within the last 3 months.

faq.q: Why does the flight need to depart 21+ days after applying?
faq.a: The embassy expects your travel dates to allow for processing (about 21 working days). Book a reservation with a departure at least 21 days out — and never a fake ticket.

faq.q: Can I get a multiple-entry visa?
faq.a: Multiple-entry tourist visas are possible in some cases, but eligibility varies. Ask at the embassy about current rules for Nepal.

faq.q: Do I still need the e-Arrival Card after I get the visa?

faq.q: Do Filipinos need a visa for Korea?

faq.q: How much is the visa fee?

faq.q: Do I need bank statements?
faq.a: The current tourist checklist lists a bank certificate, rather than a separate bank-statement item for ordinary employees. This is not a blanket exemption from financial evidence: follow your category and any additional request. Bank certificate: issued in your name within the last 3 months, showing account name, number, type, opening date, current balance and 6-month average daily balance (ADB).

faq.q: How long does it take?
faq.a: Effective 2026-10-01: ordinary C-3 processing is 12 working days; express applications remain 5 working days. Check express eligibility separately. Approval and entry are not guaranteed. Additional documents may be requested; the processing period may be recalculated after submission.

faq.q: Where do I apply?
faq.a: Submit through KVAC in the Philippines. Check the current KVAC instructions before visiting; the Embassy does not receive ordinary applications directly. If using an agency, choose from the Embassy’s current designated-agency list and confirm its submission arrangements.

faq.q: What is the separate KVAC service fee?
faq.a: KVAC charges PHP 1,000 per applicant, effective 2026-08-25. Pay in cash; this is separate from any Embassy visa issuance fee and optional agency or delivery charges. Fees are non-refundable, regardless of the decision.

faq.q: When can I collect my passport?
faq.a: Visit KVAC on the next working day after receiving its SMS notification. For personal collection, bring your valid government ID and the application receipt with barcode. A third-party collector needs additional authorization documents; check KVAC instructions.

faq.q: Must I buy flights and book a hotel before applying?
faq.a: No. KVAC says a tentative flight date and hotel name are sufficient; confirmed flight tickets and hotel reservations are not required for the application.

faq.q: Is there a fixed minimum bank balance?
faq.a: KVAC does not set a fixed minimum balance. Your funds must cover your intended stay. This does not remove the financial-document requirements for your application category.

faq.q: Do Uzbekistani citizens need a visa for Korea?

faq.q: Where do I find the accredited agencies?
faq.a: The official list is published on the Korean Embassy in Tashkent's website. Use only agencies on that list.

faq.q: How much does it cost and how long does it take?

faq.q: Where is the embassy?

Yes — Vietnamese passport holders need a visa. Apply according to your registered residence: KVAC Hanoi, KVAC Ho Chi Minh City, or the Korean Consulate General in Da Nang. Check the current jurisdiction and appointment instructions before visiting.

faq.q: Do Vietnamese citizens need a visa for Korea?
faq.a: Ordinary Vietnamese passports are not eligible for K-ETA. For a normal mainland tourist trip, obtain a visa; K-ETA cannot replace it and is not an extra application after receiving your visa.

faq.q: How long can I stay on a tourist visa?
faq.a: Hanoi single-entry C-3-9: 30 days; follow the stay granted on your issued visa

faq.q: Where do I apply?
faq.a: Apply according to your registered residence: KVAC Hanoi, KVAC Ho Chi Minh City, or the Korean Consulate General in Da Nang. Check the current jurisdiction and appointment instructions before visiting.

faq.q: How much money do I need to prove?
faq.a: Use the checklist for your office and application category. Hanoi's current individual C-3-9 checklist requests bank statements for the latest 3 months, plus salary records for employees. Include residence and family documents when applicable; translation and certification requirements vary.

faq.q: How much is the fee?
faq.a: Short-stay single-entry visa: USD 20; multiple-entry: USD 80. KVAC Hanoi and HCMC add VND 390,000 per application, excluding optional services. Confirm the payable currency and current total at your office; the KVAC service charge is not a Da Nang consular charge.

faq.q: I'm going on a company incentive trip — simpler?
faq.a: Group travel and multiple-entry visas have their own checklists and eligibility. Do not assume a company's guarantee automatically removes your financial-document requirement.

faq.q: Do I still need the e-Arrival Card?
faq.a: A short-term tourist entering with a visa must submit the e-Arrival Card unless a separate exemption applies, such as holding a valid Korean residence card. Check the official navigator for your documents.

faq.q: Can Vietnamese travelers visit Jeju without a visa?
faq.a: Vietnamese ordinary-passport tourists can use the separate Jeju visa-free program for up to 30 days, subject to entry assessment. Arrive directly at Jeju from overseas by air or sea and stay on Jeju. An itinerary entering Korea through Seoul or Busan is not covered. Going to the mainland requires the appropriate visa or prior immigration permission; admission is not guaranteed.

faq.q: How long does a Korea visa take to process?
faq.a: Published individual tourist processing times are 16 working days in Hanoi and 18 working days in Ho Chi Minh City. Weekends and holidays are excluded; additional checks can take longer. These are published estimates, not guaranteed deadlines. Da Nang applicants should confirm separately.

faq.q: Do children need their own Korea visa?
faq.a: Yes — every traveler, including children, needs their own visa. A minor's application is submitted with a parent's supporting documents and proof of the family relationship.

faq.q: Do Vietnamese travelers need K-ETA as well as a visa?
faq.a: Ordinary Vietnamese passports are not eligible for K-ETA. For a normal mainland tourist trip, obtain a visa; K-ETA cannot replace it and is not an extra application after receiving your visa.

faq.q: Does a US or Japanese visa allow visa-free transit in Korea?
faq.a: A qualifying visa or residence permit for the US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand or a listed European country may allow B-2 transit for up to 30 days on an eligible onward/return route. A Japanese visa alone is not in the current third-country transit list. You need a confirmed departure within 30 days and must meet immigration-history, routing and visa-document conditions; merely owning a visa or taking a Vietnam–Korea round trip is insufficient. Verify your complete itinerary with immigration and the airline.
